name: SCAI
subtitle: From field reports to useful answers.
summary: An AI-powered field supervision assistant for Osmani & Company, connecting incoming reports with searchable operational knowledge.
problem: Daily field reports arrive through different channels and formats. Making that information useful means more than extracting text: the system needs to connect reports to the right sites and people, preserve context, and make the information retrievable.
contribution: I work across the system: n8n ingestion workflows, AI-assisted document processing, the PostgreSQL and vector data layer, agent orchestration, APIs, and the frontend. The pipeline brings together WhatsApp reports, company email, and scanned letters.
decisions: Use vision-LLM document processing to handle scanned material alongside text-based reports.
Combine structured records in PostgreSQL with embeddings and Qdrant retrieval, so agent answers can draw on the relevant report context.
Build LangGraph-based conversational workflows that resolve site and employee references and help management explore productivity trends and bottlenecks.
Treat latency, memory, and reliability as part of the engineering work, alongside the ingestion and user interface.
note: This is a professional project. This overview describes my responsibilities at a high level; it does not reproduce internal reports, client data, or private source code.
outcome: An ongoing field-supervision system connecting report ingestion, retrieval, and management-facing conversations. My work includes production reliability and latency tuning.

name: Clarimo AI
subtitle: Give an idea something to stand on.
summary: A startup research and validation platform that connects problem discovery, competitor research, customer insights, and launch planning.
problem: An early-stage idea comes with a lot of unknowns: who needs it, what already exists, and which assumptions deserve a closer look. Clarimo brings those questions into a connected research workflow.
contribution: I built startup-validation functionality and designed a semantic data pipeline over Reddit, Product Hunt, GitHub, and app-marketplace data. The pipeline uses embeddings, filtering, clustering, and ranking to turn source material into structured insights.
decisions: Separate problem discovery, validation, competitor intelligence, and launch planning into distinct workflows.
Use semantic filtering and clustering to organize related source material before presenting research outputs.
Connect the React and TypeScript interface to FastAPI services and MongoDB-backed application data.
note: Clarimo was a team project. The work described here focuses on my contribution; repository documentation describes the wider product.
outcome: A working startup-research platform spanning discovery through go-to-market planning. AI-generated research still needs human review and source verification.

name: Jadeed
subtitle: An interface for an AI-first product.
summary: A dedicated Next.js frontend connecting AI chat, project workflows, code editing, and document generation with Django APIs.
problem: An AI-first SaaS platform needed a dedicated frontend for workflows that included authentication, project management, AI conversation, and long-running document generation.
contribution: I proposed and built a Next.js frontend from scratch, replacing the original Django-based UI approach. I developed reusable components and integrated authentication, role-based access, AI chat, GitHub APIs, Monaco Editor, and Django REST endpoints.
decisions: Build reusable UI components around authentication, project workflows, and AI interactions.
Make authorization and backend integration part of the interface architecture.
Trace long-running generation failures beyond the frontend: I diagnosed and resolved NGINX timeout limits affecting AI document generation.
note: This was a completed professional role. This overview focuses on my engineering contribution.
outcome: A dedicated Next.js product interface with integrated AI workflows, and a production timeout issue resolved across the application boundary.

name: Website Verification Agent
subtitle: Less checking. More knowing.
summary: Batch website checks for availability, redirects, and brand presence, with structured results and exports.
problem: Checking a list of websites manually involves repetitive work: open a URL, follow redirects, identify the company, and capture a result that someone else can use.
contribution: I built an automation agent with n8n, OpenAI, and custom response processing, integrated Google Sheets, and deployed the system using Railway and Vercel. The interface supports manual entries, CSV uploads, and bulk input.
decisions: Separate website availability, redirect detection, and brand presence into explicit checks.
Provide progress feedback during batch validation and export results as CSV or JSON.
Use title, metadata, headings, and page content as signals for brand presence.
note: Brand presence is a heuristic, not proof that a website is legitimate. Network failures and inaccessible pages need to remain distinguishable from negative matches.
outcome: A batch verification workflow with progress tracking and reusable output, built for the S&P Global AI Automate hackathon.

name: Jarvis Voice Assistant
subtitle: A conversation that can take action.
summary: A voice-controlled assistant connecting spoken requests with calendar, email, weather, and web tools.
problem: A voice assistant becomes useful when it can turn a spoken request into the right tool call and return a clear response.
contribution: I built a Jarvis-style assistant using n8n for orchestration, ElevenLabs for speech input and output, and Groq-hosted LLMs for reasoning and tool-response structuring.
decisions: Connect calendar, email, weather, and web-search tools behind a conversational interface.
Use webhooks to connect speech interactions with the orchestration workflow.
Support actions such as creating, updating, and cancelling meetings, alongside email drafts and live information queries.
note: This page is a project overview, not a live voice-agent demo. No microphone or account permissions are requested.
outcome: A working voice-driven tool workflow across communication, scheduling, and information retrieval.

name: FYP Handbook Assistant
subtitle: Answers with a paper trail.
summary: A retrieval assistant for the FAST NUCES final-year project handbook, grounded in the handbook text.
problem: Students need to locate specific rules and requirements in a long handbook without losing the context of the original policy.
contribution: I built a handbook-focused retrieval pipeline and a lightweight interface for natural-language questions. It combines semantic search with lexical re-ranking to retrieve relevant passages.
decisions: Index handbook content using sentence embeddings and FAISS.
Re-rank candidates with lexical signals to improve relevance.
Keep answers grounded in retrieved handbook text and make the source context available.
note: The assistant depends on the handbook version it indexes. It should not be treated as a substitute for current university policy.
outcome: An end-to-end ingestion, embedding, retrieval, and answer workflow with a Streamlit interface.

name: GoLocal Guide
subtitle: Discover a place. Plan the visit.
summary: A Pakistan-focused tourism platform with separate tourist, guide, business, and admin experiences.
problem: Travel discovery and booking involve different participants, each needing a workflow designed around their role.
contribution: I built the tourist panel across frontend and backend, including booking features, personalized dashboards, and itinerary planning. I also created the landing page and login and signup flows.
decisions: Separate user experiences for tourists, guides, businesses, and administrators.
Connect discovery and booking actions to the tourist dashboard.
Build the entry experience around a responsive landing page and clear account flows.
note: This was a team project. My ownership was the tourist panel and the entry flows, rather than every panel in the platform.
outcome: An integrated tourist experience within a multi-role local tourism platform.

name: Word Ladder Adventure
subtitle: One letter. A different path.
summary: A word puzzle exploring uniform-cost, A*, and greedy best-first search through playable transformations.
problem: Search algorithms are easier to understand when their paths become something you can play with.
contribution: I built the React interface and FastAPI backend for a word-ladder game. The backend supports UCS, A*, and greedy best-first search, with hints, difficulty levels, and session scoring.
decisions: Expose different pathfinding strategies through one word transformation problem.
Keep session scores in memory for the project scope.
Separate the React frontend from the Python search service.
note: In-memory sessions are temporary and do not provide durable player accounts.
outcome: A playable word puzzle demonstrating multiple search strategies.

name: ERPNext Complaint Management
subtitle: A clearer path from issue to resolution.
summary: An internal complaint-management module built with ERPNext and Frappe during the Osmani internship.
problem: Internal complaints need a consistent way to enter the system, move through a workflow, and remain visible to the people responsible.
contribution: I learned ERPNext and Frappe and translated business requirements into a complaint-management module with forms, workflows, reports, and notifications.
decisions: Model complaint records with Frappe DocTypes and appropriate constraints.
Use the existing ERP framework for forms and workflow behavior.
Test the module within its ERPNext integration.
note: This overview concerns the internship module; it does not expose company complaint records.
outcome: An internal complaint-management module built within ERPNext.
